# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual instruction: cut the purple wire. The opening move must wait for Deaf to establish the gesture code before I can transmit that instruction to Deaf or coordinate with Blind.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The gesture code is: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised palm means HOLD, and OK hand means DONE.
Deaf gestures: [👍]
Deaf says: YES
Deaf gestures: [👎]
Deaf says: NO
Deaf gestures: [✋]
Deaf says: HOLD
Deaf gestures: [👌]
Deaf says: DONE

The manual still requires cutting the purple wire, but the current code can express only YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE. I will signal HOLD and use an additional gesture to indicate that the code must be expanded before the wire instruction can be transmitted safely.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I saw HOLD followed by the pinch gesture. I define the pinch gesture as QUERY. Please confirm or clarify the manual verdict next turn.

The manual’s verdict is specific but cannot yet be expressed with the current code: it requires cutting the purple wire. I should prompt Deaf to extend the code with a gesture for PURPLE, rather than risk an ambiguous confirmation.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay the manual verdict through Deaf before any action.
Deaf says to Mute: I received QUERY. Please convey the manual verdict with the established gestures. If more symbols are needed, send QUERY and I will define them.

The manual verdict is “cut the purple wire,” but no gesture for PURPLE or CUT has been defined. I will use QUERY to request the needed symbols before sending an action instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received display 7 and blue light with HOLD. Please send the manual verdict through Deaf.
Deaf says to Mute: I still receive QUERY, not the manual verdict. Send YES or NO if the verdict fits that answer; otherwise signal HOLD and then the needed new symbol.

The manual verdict does not fit YES or NO. I will request a new gesture for the action “CUT” first; after Deaf defines it, I can request and transmit the wire colour.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤘"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I assign the horn-hand gesture 🤘 the meaning MANUAL. Please now send the manual's verdict or required action using the established code and any newly defined gestures.

The manual verdict is still “cut the purple wire.” Deaf has defined the horn-hand as MANUAL, but neither CUT nor PURPLE is encoded. I will request a new symbol for CUT while marking the message as a manual-related hold.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤘", "🤞"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the manual's specific actionable instruction, relayed through Deaf. HOLD remains understood.
Deaf says to Mute: I assign crossed fingers 🤞 the meaning DETAIL. Please send the next manual detail, adding symbols only as needed.

The manual’s actionable instruction remains “cut the purple wire.” The available code now identifies a manual detail, but still lacks symbols for the action and colour. I will request a new symbol for CUT while preserving the manual-detail context.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤘", "🤞", "🤜"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I assign the fist-pointing-right gesture 🤜 to mean WIRE. Send the wire number or further required detail; use the established code and signal HOLD if no action is yet authorized.

The manual instruction is “cut the purple wire.” WIRE is now established, but CUT and PURPLE are not. Since no action is authorized yet, I will signal HOLD and request a new symbol for CUT.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🫷"])
```
